evidence:
Source nesting is verified; workload adequacy is not measured. I opened the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 12 (number 11) requires agent, verifier, liveness and judge timeouts to be long enough and nested. Internal Quality Checks row 12 says 'inner < outer, sum of judges < verifier'; it is interpretation, not an override of the shipped staged profile. Deterministic Checks rows 29, 33 and 36 cover judge schema, suite nesting and liveness orchestration. The frozen Harbor quality-checks.md:50-51 explicitly requires arithmetic plus realistic build adequacy; staged-task-contract.md:111 supplies the canonical 1500/11100/13200 budgets.

All task references below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task. I parsed every one of the five judge.toml files, not a sample. tests/gates/render/judge.toml:4 and tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:4 each say 'timeout = 600'; tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:4 says 'timeout = 9000'; tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:4 and tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:4 each say 'timeout = 900'. tests/test.sh:207 uses '--max-concurrent-agent 1', so summing within each suite is necessary. tests/test.sh:213 and :224 set gates 1500 and scored 11100. Fresh read-only arithmetic: 600 + 600 = 1200 < 1500 (300 seconds spare); 9000 + 900 + 900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 spare); 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 spare). Each individual judge is also below its suite budget, and all judge limits sum to 12000 < 13200. task.toml:18, :21 and :27 set agent 7200, environment build 600 and verifier 13200 seconds. These arithmetic checks pass.

Liveness was inspected separately. tests/test.sh:42-58 and :115-124 probe /api/health and then / with 'urlopen(url, timeout=2).read()', 120 iterations and 0.25-second sleeps. This is a retry count, not a hard 30-second wall-clock bound: two timed-out requests per iteration can consume about 510 seconds plus process overhead. The analogous restart loop is at :130-146 and :170-182, preceded by up to five seconds of old-process polling at :155-157; tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:11 and :39 impose an outer 55-second subprocess timeout. I do not claim that the retry count alone proves a conforming app exceeds a budget: environment/instructions/integration.md:5 requires successful prompt health responses, and the actual golden restart completed in 5.5284269389812835 seconds. I also do not characterize the nominal 30 seconds as a measured or strict bound. tests/test.sh and tests/tools/restart_mcp.py are byte-identical to their frozen canonical template copies, as are both Dockerfiles; task.toml's timeout values and every judge timeout also match the canonical values. No task-specific timeout drift was found or changed.

The source workload is substantial but structured: all five judge files contain respectively 1 render, 1 constraints, 64 functional, 7 polish and 6 visual outcomes. tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:9, :102-113 calls for 23 shared protocols executed once in six phases, bounded retries and batched timed observations. Its 23 'About ... UI actions' planning figures sum to 450, explicitly estimates rather than measured actions or score limits. :113 itself says the batching 'does not establish full judge completion time'. The remaining prompts require gate operations, keyboard navigation and desktop/mobile/theme review; I inspected all of them and app_context.md. No configured LLM judge transcript showing their completion was supplied.

I verified SHA256 for all 50 frozen task files and all 34 frozen rule/template files against qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/manifest.json, whose input_sha256 is the assigned hash. The raw-evidence-index.json explicitly identifies the available run as direct scripted browser observations, with no full configured verifier, target model, Oracle or measured judge workload. I independently opened the raw RESULTS.json and copied launcher instead of relying on a prior verdict. qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-repair3/golden/run-golden-20260930-092021/RESULTS.json SHA256 is ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09, matching the index. Its :3 and :5 say paid_provider=false and browser_driver='direct pinned Playwright'; :13113 records wall_seconds=118.82740359200398 and :13114 says oracle_score_claimed=false. drivers/launch_workflow.py:34 labels this direct Playwright; :43 executes node run_workflow.cjs, :69 invokes the restart MCP, and :83 executes node surface_flow.cjs. It does not execute the full RewardKit judge suite. Thus its approximately 119 seconds is product/driver timing, not LLM judge timing or a cold Docker build. The required current-run runtime-evidence.json is absent. No raw cold-build measurement or target-builder completion under 7200 seconds is provided in this evidence set. Both Dockerfiles perform networked package installation, and the verifier also installs Chromium, so source inspection alone cannot establish a realistic cold-build upper bound.

qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:25 explicitly says workload is measured and scripted Playwright duration is not LLM judge duration. qc/README.md:25-27 and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:31 require hash-bound workload logs and say runtime gaps block clearance. Accordingly this is Not exercised with risk=true and severity=null for required missing evidence, run_verdict PARTIAL for the passing source arithmetic and limited scripted timing. No actual judge overrun, cold-build overrun, or target-builder failure is asserted.
counterexample: Conforming alternative considered: a compliant editor with accessible composite menus and a library drawer is expressly allowed by tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:43-47 and functional/prompt.md:11. It can require different control discovery and keyboard actions from the golden's scripted selectors, so the golden's 118.827-second driver time cannot establish that its real 900-second Polish or 9000-second Functional judge completes. This is an unexecuted workload challenge, not a claim that this UI actually times out. Broken-app false-clearance witness: a dead Run implementation fails Render and returns early at tests/test.sh:218-221, so even a very fast full process run against that app would leave the 77 scored outcomes unexercised and could falsely clear 'timeouts fit' if runtime alone were accepted. A completion measurement must include the full configured work, with coverage and returned results. No unobserved application score is claimed.
suggested_fix: Keep canonical settings unchanged. Supply current-hash raw logs from an authorized cold build and complete configured verifier/LLM judge run on the golden, including startup, each judge and suite duration, result completeness, overhead and failures; record the real command and artifact hashes in runtime-evidence.json. Supply builder timing evidence separately for the agent allowance. If measured workload exceeds a limit, reduce redundant task-specific browser work while preserving coverage and independent credit, then freeze and review the new candidate.
